# Archive as Design Employee

## Canonical thesis
An archive becomes institutional infrastructure when it is retrievable, interpretable, rights-aware, and capable of changing a live creative decision.

## Complete editorial sequence
A room full of garments is not automatically an archive, and an archive is not automatically useful. The institution begins when objects and records can answer a new question without severing evidence from interpretation.

Tapestry’s public filing states that designers use product-design archives as a resource for concepts. The Gianfranco Ferré Research Center presents another model: an archive organized for research and transmission. Neither source proves that every archive produces good design. They establish a narrower point—the archive can be deliberately operated as creative infrastructure.

### 01 · RETRIEVE — Can the right record be found?
Identifiers, dates, makers, materials, controlled vocabulary, file relationships, and search pathways determine whether memory is available at the moment of decision.

Evidence: VERIFIED · S21, S35

### 02 · READ — Can someone understand why it matters?
A sketch, fitting note, failed sample, or garment becomes more useful when the record preserves the question it answered—not only what it looks like.

Evidence: INFERENCE · S21, S22

### 03 · TRANSFORM — Can the archive generate difference?
The strongest use is not literal revival. It is recovery of a method, constraint, construction problem, or unresolved question that can be recomposed for a new context.

Evidence: PROPOSAL · S21, S22

### 04 · CITE — Can the new work show its lineage?
Source identifiers, rights decisions, credits, and transformation notes let inspiration remain accountable. Citation does not weaken originality; it distinguishes research from extraction.

Evidence: PROPOSAL · S23, S24

## Counterargument
An archive can consolidate authority as easily as it distributes knowledge. Who receives access, who describes the objects, and whose labor appears in the metadata determines what the institution can remember.

## Fieldwork
1. Select one current design question—not a favorite old object.
2. Retrieve three records that answer it in different ways.
3. Record the evidentiary fact and your interpretation in separate fields.
4. Define what may be reused, what may only be linked, and what requires permission.

## Release gates
Recording/performance, any bespoke photography, participant verification, labor and contract review where flagged, and RN owner-final approval.
